body.en: A limit asks: as \( x \) gets closer and closer to some value, what does \( f(x) \) get closer and closer to? This is precalculus' bridge into calculus — the same machinery that eventually defines the derivative and the integral, here used to make sense of behavior a function's formula doesn't show directly.
body.ar: A النهاية asks: as \( x \) gets closer and closer to some value, what does \( f(x) \) get closer and closer to? This is precalculus' bridge into التفاضل والتكامل — the same machinery that eventually defines the المشتقة and the التكامل, here used to make sense of behavior a الدالة's الصيغة doesn't show directly.

body.en: We write \[ \lim_{x\to a}f(x)=L \] to mean: as \( x \) approaches \( a \) (from either side, without necessarily equaling \( a \)), \( f(x) \) approaches \( L \). When \( f \) is a polynomial or rational function and \( a \) is in its domain, the limit is found simply by direct substitution: \( \lim_{x\to a}f(x)=f(a) \).
body.ar: We write \[ \lim_{x\to a}f(x)=L \] to mean: as \( x \) approaches \( a \) (from either side, without necessarily equaling \( a \)), \( f(x) \) approaches \( L \). عندما \( f \) is a كثيرة الحدود or rational الدالة and \( a \) is in its المجال, the النهاية is found simply by direct substitution: \( \lim_{x\to a}f(x)=f(a) \).

body.en:
Find \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to3}\big(x^2-2x+1\big) \).

Since this polynomial is defined everywhere, substitute directly: \[ \lim_{x\to3}\big(x^2-2x+1\big)=3^2-2(3)+1=9-6+1=4. \]
body.ar:
Find \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to3}\big(x^2-2x+1\big) \).

Since this كثيرة الحدود is defined everywhere, عوّض directly: \[ \lim_{x\to3}\big(x^2-2x+1\big)=3^2-2(3)+1=9-6+1=4. \]

body.en: If direct substitution gives \( \tfrac{0}{0} \), the limit isn't automatically \( 0 \), undefined, or anything else — it's an indeterminate form, meaning more work is needed. For rational functions, the usual fix is to factor and cancel the common factor causing the zero, then substitute again.
body.ar: If direct substitution gives \( \tfrac{0}{0} \), the النهاية isn't automatically \( 0 \), undefined, or anything else — it's an indeterminate form, meaning more work is needed. For rational الدوال, the usual fix is to factor and cancel the common factor causing the zero, then عوّض again.

body.en:
Find \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to2}\dfrac{x^2-4}{x-2} \).

Direct substitution gives \( \tfrac{4-4}{2-2}=\tfrac00 \) — indeterminate. Factor the numerator: \[ \frac{x^2-4}{x-2}=\frac{(x-2)(x+2)}{x-2}=x+2 \quad(x\neq2). \] The canceled form agrees with the original everywhere except exactly at \( x=2 \) — which is fine, since a limit only cares about values near \( x=2 \), never at it. Now substitute: \[ \lim_{x\to2}\frac{x^2-4}{x-2}=\lim_{x\to2}(x+2)=2+2=4. \]
body.ar:
Find \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to2}\dfrac{x^2-4}{x-2} \).

Direct substitution gives \( \tfrac{4-4}{2-2}=\tfrac00 \) — indeterminate. Factor the numerator: \[ \frac{x^2-4}{x-2}=\frac{(x-2)(x+2)}{x-2}=x+2 \quad(x\neq2). \] The canceled form agrees with the original everywhere except exactly at \( x=2 \) — which is fine, since a النهاية only cares about values near \( x=2 \), never at it. Now عوّض: \[ \lim_{x\to2}\frac{x^2-4}{x-2}=\lim_{x\to2}(x+2)=2+2=4. \]

body.en: \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x) \) describes what \( f(x) \) approaches as \( x \) grows without bound. For a rational function \( \dfrac{p(x)}{q(x)} \), the result depends only on comparing the degrees of \( p \) and \( q \).
body.ar: \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x) \) describes what \( f(x) \) approaches as \( x \) grows without bound. For a rational الدالة \( \dfrac{p(x)}{q(x)} \), the result depends only on comparing the degrees of \( p \) and \( q \).

label.en: ▲ Theorem 6.1 — Limits at infinity for rational functions
label.ar: ▲ مبرهنة 6.1 — النهايات at infinity for rational الدوال

body.en:
For \( f(x)=\dfrac{p(x)}{q(x)} \) with \( \deg p=m \), \( \deg q=n \), leading coefficients \( a \) (of \( p \)) and \( b \) (of \( q \)):

  • If \( m < n \): \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)=0 \).
  • If \( m=n \): \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)=\dfrac{a}{b} \) (ratio of leading coefficients).
  • If \( m > n \): the limit does not exist as a finite number — \( f(x)\to\pm\infty \).
body.ar:
For \( f(x)=\dfrac{p(x)}{q(x)} \) with \( \deg p=m \), \( \deg q=n \), leading المعاملات \( a \) (of \( p \)) and \( b \) (of \( q \)):

  • If \( m < n \): \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)=0 \).
  • If \( m=n \): \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)=\dfrac{a}{b} \) (ratio of leading المعاملات).
  • If \( m > n \): the النهاية does not exist as a finite number — \( f(x)\to\pm\infty \).

body.en: Divide numerator and denominator by \( x^n \) (the denominator's highest power): every term of the form \( \dfrac{c\,x^k}{x^n}=c\,x^{k-n} \) with \( k < n \) has a negative exponent and shrinks to \( 0 \) as \( x\to\infty \) (the same reasoning as \( r^n\to0 \) for \( |r| < 1 \) in Theorem 3.2, applied to \( 1/x\to0 \)). What survives depends on how the top and bottom's own highest powers compare after dividing: if \( m < n \), every term in the numerator vanishes, leaving \( \tfrac{0}{b}=0 \); if \( m=n \), the only surviving terms are the leading coefficients themselves, \( \tfrac{a}{b} \); if \( m > n \), a positive power of \( x \) survives in the numerator after dividing by \( x^n \), and that power grows without bound. \( \blacksquare \)
body.ar: Divide numerator and denominator by \( x^n \) (the denominator's highest power): every term of the form \( \dfrac{c\,x^k}{x^n}=c\,x^{k-n} \) with \( k < n \) has a negative exponent and shrinks to \( 0 \) as \( x\to\infty \) (the same reasoning as \( r^n\to0 \) for \( |r| < 1 \) in مبرهنة 3.2, applied to \( 1/x\to0 \)). What survives depends on how the top and bottom's own highest powers compare after dividing: if \( m < n \), every term in the numerator vanishes, leaving \( \tfrac{0}{b}=0 \); if \( m=n \), the only surviving terms are the leading المعاملات themselves, \( \tfrac{a}{b} \); if \( m > n \), a positive power of \( x \) survives in the numerator after dividing by \( x^n \), and that power grows without bound. \( \blacksquare \)

label.en: Worked example 6.C — Limits at infinity, all three cases
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.C — النهايات at infinity, all three cases

body.en:
Evaluate each as \( x\to\infty \):

\[ \text{(i) } \frac{5x+1}{2x^2+3}\to0 \quad(\deg\,\text{num}=1<\deg\,\text{den}=2) \]

\[ \text{(ii) } \frac{3x^2+2x}{x^2-5}\to\frac{3}{1}=3 \quad(\text{equal degrees, ratio of leading coefficients}) \]

\[ \text{(iii) } \frac{2x^3+1}{x^2}\to\infty \quad(\deg\,\text{num}=3>\deg\,\text{den}=2) \]

body.en: A function \( f \) is continuous at \( x=a \) if all three of these hold: \( f(a) \) is defined, \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to a}f(x) \) exists, and \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=f(a) \). Informally: the graph has no hole, jump, or break at \( x=a \).
body.ar: A الدالة \( f \) is continuous at \( x=a \) if all three of these hold: \( f(a) \) is defined, \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to a}f(x) \) exists, and \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=f(a) \). Informally: the التمثيل البياني has no hole, jump, or break at \( x=a \).

label.en: Worked example 6.D — Enforcing continuity with unknown constants
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.D — Enforcing continuity with unknown constants

body.en:
Find the value of \( c \) that makes the function \( g(x) \) continuous for all real numbers:

\[ g(x) = \begin{cases} cx + 4, & x < 2 \\ x^2 - c, & x \geq 2 \end{cases} \]

Step 1: Compute left-hand and right-hand limits at the boundary \( x = 2 \):
\[ \lim_{x\to 2^-} g(x) = c(2) + 4 = 2c + 4 \] \[ \lim_{x\to 2^+} g(x) = 2^2 - c = 4 - c \]

Step 2: Equate left and right limits (Definition 6.4):
\[ 2c + 4 = 4 - c \implies 3c = 0 \implies \mathbf{c = 0}. \]

Step 3: Verify: For \( c = 0 \), \( \lim_{x\to 2^-} g(x) = 4 \), \( \lim_{x\to 2^+} g(x) = 4 \), and \( g(2) = 4 \). Continuous everywhere ✓.
body.ar:
Find the value of \( c \) that makes the الدالة \( g(x) \) continuous for all real numbers:

\[ g(x) = \begin{cases} cx + 4, & x < 2 \\ x^2 - c, & x \geq 2 \end{cases} \]

Step 1: Compute left-hand and right-hand النهايات at the boundary \( x = 2 \):
\[ \lim_{x\to 2^-} g(x) = c(2) + 4 = 2c + 4 \] \[ \lim_{x\to 2^+} g(x) = 2^2 - c = 4 - c \]

Step 2: Equate left and right النهايات (تعريف 6.4):
\[ 2c + 4 = 4 - c \implies 3c = 0 \implies \mathbf{c = 0}. \]

Step 3: Verify: For \( c = 0 \), \( \lim_{x\to 2^-} g(x) = 4 \), \( \lim_{x\to 2^+} g(x) = 4 \), and \( g(2) = 4 \). Continuous everywhere ✓.

body.en:
0/0 is NOT 0 or Undefined: When direct substitution gives \(\dfrac{0}{0}\), this is an indeterminate form. It signals that algebraic work is required (factoring, rationalizing, or simplifying) to determine the true limit value.

Hole vs Value: A limit \(\lim_{x\to a}f(x)\) describes the behavior of \(f(x)\) as \(x\) gets arbitrarily close to \(a\), completely independent of whether \(f(a)\) is defined.

One-Sided Agreement: For the two-sided limit \(\lim_{x\to a}f(x)\) to exist, the left-hand limit \(\lim_{x\to a^-}f(x)\) and right-hand limit \(\lim_{x\to a^+}f(x)\) must both exist and be equal.
body.ar:
0/0 is NOT 0 or Undefined: عندما direct substitution gives \(\dfrac{0}{0}\), this is an indeterminate form. It signals that algebraic work is required (factoring, rationalizing, or simplifying) to حدّد true النهاية value.

Hole vs Value: A النهاية \(\lim_{x\to a}f(x)\) describes the behavior of \(f(x)\) as \(x\) gets arbitrarily close to \(a\), completely independent of whether \(f(a)\) is defined.

One-Sided Agreement: For the two-sided النهاية \(\lim_{x\to a}f(x)\) to exist, the left-hand النهاية \(\lim_{x\to a^-}f(x)\) and right-hand النهاية \(\lim_{x\to a^+}f(x)\) must both exist and be equal.

question.en: Evaluate the limit using algebraic conjugate rationalization: \[ \lim_{x\to 4} \frac{\sqrt{x} - 2}{x - 4} \]
question.ar: احسب قيمة النهاية using algebraic conjugate rationalization: \[ \lim_{x\to 4} \frac{\sqrt{x} - 2}{x - 4} \]

solution.en:
Step 1: Check form upon direct substitution:
\[ \frac{\sqrt{4} - 2}{4 - 4} = \frac{0}{0} \quad (\text{indeterminate form}). \]

Step 2: Multiply by the conjugate of the numerator:
\[ \lim_{x\to 4}\frac{(\sqrt{x}-2)(\sqrt{x}+2)}{(x-4)(\sqrt{x}+2)} = \lim_{x\to 4}\frac{(\sqrt{x})^2 - 2^2}{(x-4)(\sqrt{x}+2)} = \lim_{x\to 4}\frac{x - 4}{(x-4)(\sqrt{x}+2)}. \]

Step 3: Cancel the common factor \( (x - 4) \) for \( x eq 4 \):
\[ \lim_{x\to 4}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}+2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{4}+2} = \frac{1}{2 + 2} = \mathbf{\frac{1}{4}}. \]
solution.ar:
Step 1: Check form upon direct substitution:
\[ \frac{\sqrt{4} - 2}{4 - 4} = \frac{0}{0} \quad (\text{indeterminate form}). \]

Step 2: Multiply بتطبيق conjugate of the numerator:
\[ \lim_{x\to 4}\frac{(\sqrt{x}-2)(\sqrt{x}+2)}{(x-4)(\sqrt{x}+2)} = \lim_{x\to 4}\frac{(\sqrt{x})^2 - 2^2}{(x-4)(\sqrt{x}+2)} = \lim_{x\to 4}\frac{x - 4}{(x-4)(\sqrt{x}+2)}. \]

Step 3: Cancel the common حلّل \( (x - 4) \) for \( x eq 4 \):
\[ \lim_{x\to 4}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}+2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{4}+2} = \frac{1}{2 + 2} = \mathbf{\frac{1}{4}}. \]

hints.en: Multiply by the conjugate of the numerator: \(\lim_{x\to 4}\frac{(\sqrt{x}-2)(\sqrt{x}+2)}{(x-4)(\sqrt{x}+2)} = \lim_{x\to 4}\frac{(\sqrt{x})^2 - 2^2}{(x-4)(\sqrt{x}+2)} = \lim_{x\to 4}\frac{x - 4}{(x-4)(\sqrt{x}+2)}\).

question.en: Evaluate the limit of the rational expression by factoring: \[ \lim_{x\to 3} \frac{x^3 - 27}{x^2 - 2x - 3} \]
question.ar: احسب قيمة النهاية of the rational expression by حلّلing: \[ \lim_{x\to 3} \frac{x^3 - 27}{x^2 - 2x - 3} \]

solution.en:
Step 1: Direct substitution check:
\[ \frac{3^3 - 27}{3^2 - 2(3) - 3} = \frac{27 - 27}{9 - 6 - 3} = \frac{0}{0} \quad (\text{indeterminate}). \]

Step 2: Factor numerator using difference of cubes:
\[ x^3 - 27 = (x - 3)(x^2 + 3x + 9) \]

Step 3: Factor denominator:
\[ x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x - 3)(x + 1) \]

Step 4: Cancel the common factor \( (x - 3) \) and evaluate:
\[ \lim_{x\to 3}\frac{(x-3)(x^2 + 3x + 9)}{(x-3)(x+1)} = \lim_{x\to 3}\frac{x^2 + 3x + 9}{x + 1} = \frac{3^2 + 3(3) + 9}{3 + 1} = \frac{9 + 9 + 9}{4} = \mathbf{\frac{27}{4}}. \]
solution.ar:
Step 1: Direct substitution check:
\[ \frac{3^3 - 27}{3^2 - 2(3) - 3} = \frac{27 - 27}{9 - 6 - 3} = \frac{0}{0} \quad (\text{indeterminate}). \]

Step 2: حلّل numerator using dإذا كانference of cubes:
\[ x^3 - 27 = (x - 3)(x^2 + 3x + 9) \]

Step 3: حلّل denominator:
\[ x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x - 3)(x + 1) \]

Step 4: Cancel the common حلّل \( (x - 3) \) and احسب قيمة:
\[ \lim_{x\to 3}\frac{(x-3)(x^2 + 3x + 9)}{(x-3)(x+1)} = \lim_{x\to 3}\frac{x^2 + 3x + 9}{x + 1} = \frac{3^2 + 3(3) + 9}{3 + 1} = \frac{9 + 9 + 9}{4} = \mathbf{\frac{27}{4}}. \]

hints.en: Factor numerator using difference of cubes: \(x^3 - 27 = (x - 3)(x^2 + 3x + 9)\) Factor denominator: \(x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x - 3)(x + 1)\).
hints.ar: حلّل numerator using dإذا كانference of cubes: \(x^3 - 27 = (x - 3)(x^2 + 3x + 9)\) حلّل denominator: \(x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x - 3)(x + 1)\).

Cancel the common حلّل \((x - 3)\) and احسب قيمة: \(\lim_{x\to 3}\frac{(x-3)(x^2 + 3x + 9)}{(x-3)(x+1)} = \lim_{x\to 3}\frac{x^2 + 3x + 9}{x + 1} = \frac{3^2 + 3(3) + 9}{3 + 1} = \frac{9 + 9 + 9}{4}\).

question.en: Determine the value of the constant \( k \) for which the function \( f(x) \) is continuous at \( x = 2 \): \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} kx^2 + 2x, & x \leq 2 \\ 3x + k, & x > 2 \end{cases} \]
question.ar: حدّد value of the constant \( k \) for which the function \( f(x) \) is continuous at \( x = 2 \): \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} kx^2 + 2x, & x \leq 2 \\ 3x + k, & x > 2 \end{cases} \]

solution.en:
Step 1: Apply the definition of continuity at a point (Definition 6.4):
Continuity requires \( \lim_{x\to 2^-} f(x) = \lim_{x\to 2^+} f(x) = f(2) \).

Step 2: Evaluate the one-sided limits:
Left-hand limit and function value: \[ \lim_{x\to 2^-} f(x) = f(2) = k(2)^2 + 2(2) = 4k + 4. \]
Right-hand limit: \[ \lim_{x\to 2^+} f(x) = 3(2) + k = 6 + k. \]

Step 3: Set them equal and solve for \( k \):
\[ 4k + 4 = 6 + k \implies 3k = 2 \implies \mathbf{k = \frac{2}{3}}. \]

Check: For \( k = 2/3 \), \( 4(2/3) + 4 = \frac{8}{3} + \frac{12}{3} = \frac{20}{3} \) and \( 6 + 2/3 = \frac{20}{3} \) ✓.
solution.ar:
Step 1: Apply the definition of continuity at a point (Definition 6.4):
Continuity requires \( \lim_{x\to 2^-} f(x) = \lim_{x\to 2^+} f(x) = f(2) \).

Step 2: احسب قيمة the one-sided limits:
Left-hand limit and function value: \[ \lim_{x\to 2^-} f(x) = f(2) = k(2)^2 + 2(2) = 4k + 4. \]
Right-hand limit: \[ \lim_{x\to 2^+} f(x) = 3(2) + k = 6 + k. \]

Step 3: Set them equal and أوجد قيمة \( k \):
\[ 4k + 4 = 6 + k \implies 3k = 2 \implies \mathbf{k = \frac{2}{3}}. \]

Check: For \( k = 2/3 \), \( 4(2/3) + 4 = \frac{8}{3} + \frac{12}{3} = \frac{20}{3} \) and \( 6 + 2/3 = \frac{20}{3} \) ✓.

question.en: Evaluate the limit at infinity involving a square root in the numerator: \[ \lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{\sqrt{9x^2 + 4x}}{2x - 1} \]
question.ar: احسب قيمة النهاية at infinity involving a square root in the numerator: \[ \lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{\sqrt{9x^2 + 4x}}{2x - 1} \]

solution.en:
Step 1: Divide numerator and denominator by \( x \) (for \( x > 0 \), \( x = \sqrt{x^2} \)):
\[ \frac{\sqrt{9x^2 + 4x}}{2x - 1} = \frac{\frac{\sqrt{9x^2 + 4x}}{\sqrt{x^2}}}{\frac{2x - 1}{x}} = \frac{\sqrt{\frac{9x^2}{x^2} + \frac{4x}{x^2}}}{2 - \frac{1}{x}} = \frac{\sqrt{9 + \frac{4}{x}}}{2 - \frac{1}{x}}. \]

Step 2: Take the limit as \( x\to\infty \):
Since \( \frac{4}{x}\to 0 \) and \( \frac{1}{x}\to 0 \):
\[ \lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{\sqrt{9 + \frac{4}{x}}}{2 - \frac{1}{x}} = \frac{\sqrt{9 + 0}}{2 - 0} = \frac{3}{2} = \mathbf{\frac{3}{2}}. \]

(Note: This also confirms that \( y = \frac{3}{2} \) is the horizontal asymptote of the function as \( x \to \infty \)).

hints.en: Direct substitution of \( x = 3 \) into the expression gives \( \frac{3^2 - 2(3) - 3}{3 - 3} = \frac{0}{0} \), which is an indeterminate form.
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( x = 3 \) ، \( \frac{3^2 - 2(3) - 3}{3 - 3} = \frac{0}{0} \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Factor the numerator: \(x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x - 3)(x + 1)\) For all \( x eq 3 \), simplify the rational expression by canceling the common factor \( (x - 3) \): \(\frac{(x - 3)(x + 1)}{x - 3} = x + 1\).
hints.ar: حلّل the numerator: \(x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x - 3)(x + 1)\) For all \( x eq 3 \), بسّط العبارة the rational expression by canceling the common حلّل \( (x - 3) \): \(\frac{(x - 3)(x + 1)}{x - 3} = x + 1\).

hints.en: Now evaluate the limit by direct substitution: \(\lim_{x \to 3} (x + 1) = 3 + 1\).
hints.ar: Now احسب قيمة النهاية by direct substitution: \(\lim_{x \to 3} (x + 1) = 3 + 1\).

solution.en:
Direct substitution of \( x = 3 \) into the expression gives \( \frac{3^2 - 2(3) - 3}{3 - 3} = \frac{0}{0} \), which is an indeterminate form.

Factor the numerator:
\[
x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x - 3)(x + 1)
\]

For all \( x \neq 3 \), simplify the rational expression by canceling the common factor \( (x - 3) \):
\[
\frac{(x - 3)(x + 1)}{x - 3} = x + 1
\]

Now evaluate the limit by direct substitution:
\[
\lim_{x \to 3} (x + 1) = 3 + 1 = 4
\]

Common misconceptions include concluding that the limit is \( 0 \) because the numerator evaluates to \( 0 \), or incorrectly believing that the limit does not exist simply because the denominator evaluates to \( 0 \) at \( x = 3 \).
solution.ar:
Direct substitution of \( x = 3 \) into the expression gives \( \frac{3^2 - 2(3) - 3}{3 - 3} = \frac{0}{0} \), which is an indeterminate form.

حلّل the numerator:
\[
x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x - 3)(x + 1)
\]

For all \( x \neq 3 \), بسّط العبارة the rational expression by canceling the common حلّل \( (x - 3) \):
\[
\frac{(x - 3)(x + 1)}{x - 3} = x + 1
\]

Now احسب قيمة النهاية by direct substitution:
\[
\lim_{x \to 3} (x + 1) = 3 + 1 = 4
\]

Common misconceptions include concluding that the limit is \( 0 \) because the numerator احسب قيمةs to \( 0 \), or incorrectly believing that the limit does not exist simply because the denominator احسب قيمةs to \( 0 \) at \( x = 3 \).
